memories.content: Specify a single representative measure that serves as the criterion for retaining, modifying, or discarding compared design alternatives.
HCI review panels verify whether clear criteria for judging design alternatives are established using the declared primary measure.
Collect process measures to diagnose interaction steps where problems occurred, alongside the primary outcome measure.
Interpret evaluation results as differences between compared design alternatives rather than as success or failure of a single prototype.
Check boundary cases to verify whether the derived design principles retain explanatory power for adjacent situations not included in the comparison.
Controlled evaluation environments do not reproduce time pressure, peer intervention, or voluntary termination conditions found in daily use.
Link anticipated participant burden with its mitigation strategies for each field user study task.
Specify the accommodations necessary for participants to access the field system and research tasks.
Specify how accessibility accommodations will be provided in the field user study.
Describe how personal identifiers will be separated from research data immediately upon collection.
List equipment to be loaned when participants lack necessary gear.
Describe the procedure for returning equipment loaned to participants.
The HCI ethics reviewer verifies that anticipated burden and mitigation strategies correspond for each field user study task.
Ensure that participants can safely return to existing work procedures if they discontinue research participation.
Specify that organizational members who decline research participation will not face disadvantages in task assignment or performance evaluation.
The user's withdrawal risk can be adequately assessed only when a safe alternative procedure exists for field tasks.
The user tends to assume that a short session also entails little burden from work interruption and exposure to a manager.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate but complementary HCI concerns: the reference frame governs comparative evaluation design and interpretation, while the compared frame governs ethical and operational protections for field-study participation. Neither frame supplies a scope-aligned counterpart to the other’s claims.

relations.reason: Both memories split one reference-only requirement into specification of the decision criterion and review of whether that criterion is clearly established.
relations.summary: A declared primary measure establishes the criterion for judging design alternatives and is subject to panel verification.

relations.reason: This diagnostic-measure requirement appears only in the reference frame and has no operational counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Process measures should accompany the primary outcome measure to locate problematic interaction steps.

relations.reason: This interpretation rule is independently useful reference-only information.
relations.summary: Evaluation results should be interpreted as differences among design alternatives, not as a single prototype’s success or failure.

relations.reason: This external-explanatory-power check appears only in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Adjacent boundary cases should test whether derived design principles retain explanatory power beyond the original comparison.

relations.reason: This limitation of evaluation ecology is a reference-only claim, distinct from the compared frame’s field-study safeguards.
relations.summary: Controlled evaluations omit daily-use conditions such as time pressure, peer intervention, and voluntary termination.

relations.reason: Both memories split one compared-only burden-control requirement into its specification and reviewer verification.
relations.summary: Anticipated burden and mitigation strategies should correspond for every field-study task and be verified by an ethics reviewer.

relations.reason: Both memories restate and elaborate one compared-only accommodation requirement.
relations.summary: Necessary accessibility accommodations and their method of provision should be specified for the field system and research tasks.

relations.reason: This data-protection procedure appears only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Personal identifiers should be separated from research data immediately upon collection.

relations.reason: This equipment-provision requirement is independently useful compared-only information.
relations.summary: Equipment to be loaned when participants lack required gear should be listed.

relations.reason: This equipment-return requirement is independently useful compared-only information.
relations.summary: A procedure should govern the return of equipment loaned to participants.

relations.reason: Both memories express linked parts of one compared-only safeguard: availability of a safe alternative and its necessity for assessing withdrawal.
relations.summary: Field participation requires a safe fallback to existing procedures, enabling meaningful assessment of withdrawal risk.

relations.reason: This protection against participation-related coercion appears only in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Organizational members who decline participation should face no disadvantage in task assignment or performance evaluation.

relations.reason: This behavioral assumption about field-study burden is independently useful compared-only information.
relations.summary: Users may wrongly infer that short sessions impose little burden from work interruption or managerial exposure.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame addresses burden mitigation, accessibility, data separation, equipment logistics, withdrawal safeguards, nonparticipant protections, and misconceptions about workplace burden.
reports.reference_only: The reference frame addresses primary and diagnostic measures, comparative interpretation, boundary-case testing, and limits of controlled environments.
